blocks.heading: Distribution and availability
blocks.text: Distribution is the process of supplying goods to businesses and, through appropriate channels, making the offering available to final customers. It includes choosing the route through intermediaries or direct supply, stock availability and fulfilment. Transport is physical movement, one activity supporting distribution. A retailer can make goods conveniently available even when a separate carrier moves them. A good channel must fit customer access, product characteristics, costs and control; having a delivery vehicle alone does not describe the full route to buyers.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Teya Pots supplies shops that sell to households, with a courier carrying the orders. The route through shops is its channel; the courier provides transport. Calling the channel a truck would confuse a business arrangement with the movement method.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why “road transport” does not fully describe Eha Pots’ distribution channel. Eha sells to shops, which sell to households; a carrier moves the pots by road.

Producer to retailer to consumer is the channel, describing the selling route. Road transport physically moves goods within it. Distribution concerns how the offer reaches customers, while transport is one supporting movement activity.
